author: Altaf Hussain Hali
edition: Hali Press, Panipat, 1924. The publisher's matter is omitted.
description: Written in 1874 by the poet and reformer Altaf Husain Hali (1837–1914), Majalis-un-Nissa is one of the first Urdu prose narratives set entirely in the home, and a founding text of the debate on women's education in South Asia. In nine evening gatherings an elderly governess, Atu-ji, answers the doubts of the young women of a Delhi household by telling the life of Zubaida Khatun: how her mother taught her to read, keep accounts and run a house; how, widowed young, she raised her son Sayyid Abbas herself; and how he travelled from Delhi to Bombay, Mecca and Istanbul. Rich in the everyday speech of Delhi women, with Hali's own glosses. Complete Urdu text from the Hali Press edition (Panipat, 1924; publisher's matter omitted), with a facing English translation, introduction and glossary.
translation_note: Faithful English translation made for this library, section by section, with translator's notes marked [TN]. Each reading section is one chapter, ending with a glossary.
